sets.no: List the pairs in a column from 1 up.

sets.q: What are ALL the factors of 46? List them smallest to largest.
sets.no: Start at 1 × the number. Test 2, 3, 4, 5… in order. Write both numbers of every pair that works. Stop when the pairs meet.

sets.q: Which cow ID number is prime?
sets.why: 137: not even, 1 + 3 + 7 = 11 (not a multiple of 3), does not end in 0 or 5, and 7 and 11 do not divide it. 137 is prime.

sets.q: What is the smallest digit you can write in the blank to make 7 _ 4 divisible by 3?
sets.why: 7 + 4 = 11. Try 0 (11), 1 (12). 12 is a multiple of 3, so the digit is 1: 714 ÷ 3 = 238.
sets.no: Add the digits you have. What do you need to reach a multiple of 3?

sets.q: LCM of 6 and 20 = ____
sets.why: Multiples of 20: 20 (÷ 6? no), 40 (no), 60 (yes). The LCM is 60.
sets.no: List the multiples of the bigger number: ×1, ×2, ×3… Stop at the first one the smaller number also divides evenly.

sets.why: Factors of 30: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. 72 ÷ 6 = 12, but 72 ÷ 10 and 72 ÷ 15 leave remainders. The GCF is 6.
sets.no: List the factors of each number. Circle the factors they share. The biggest one you circled is the GCF.

sets.q: Mom buys milk every 4 days and bread every 7 days. She bought both today. In how many days will she buy both on the same day again?
sets.why: Multiples of 7: 7, 14, 21, 28. 28 ÷ 4 = 7 ✓. The LCM is 28 days.
sets.no: List the multiples of the bigger number: ×1, ×2, ×3… Stop at the first one the smaller number also divides evenly.

sets.q: Joyce has 40 red beads and 56 blue beads. She makes identical bracelets with nothing left over. What is the greatest number of bracelets?
sets.why: Factors of 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. 56 ÷ 8 = 7. The GCF is 8 bracelets (5 red and 7 blue on each).
no: 4 is a common factor, but 8 is greater.
16 is a factor of neither 40 nor 56.
280 is the LCM, a multiple. You can't make 280 bracelets from 40 beads.

sets.q: 4 × 9 = 36, so 4 and 9 are a ________ pair of 36.
sets.why: They are a factor pair.
sets.no: Two numbers that multiply to make 36.

sets.q: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?

visual.text:
Read the story
The Sandcastle Wall
1 Clyde dug a deep moat around the sandcastle. “The waves can’t get us now,” he said.
2 “They will if the wall is too short,” Ethan said. “Pile the sand higher.”
3 Joyce dumped a bucket of wet sand on top. “Is this good?” she asked.
4 “That’s perfect!” Clyde cheered.

sets.why: Tag first: comma after asked, capital I, question mark inside.
no: Tag first needs a comma after asked.
The first spoken word needs a capital: Is.
The question mark belongs inside the closing quotation mark.

sets.why: “That’s perfect!” Clyde cheered. Cheered shows he is happy and excited.

sets.q: Tag first: what mark goes right after the tag, before the opening quotation mark? Type its name.
sets.why: A comma: Ethan said, “Pile the sand higher.”
sets.no: It is a small mark that shows a pause.
sets.hint: It is the same mark that goes inside when the tag comes last.

sets.q: Which cow ID number is composite?
sets.why: 1 + 7 + 7 = 15, a multiple of 3, so 177 = 3 × 59. It has more than two factors.

sets.q: Which digit goes in the blank to make 3 _ 5 divisible by 9?
sets.why: 3 + 5 = 8. The next multiple of 9 is 9, so the digit is 1: 315 ÷ 9 = 35.
sets.no: Add the digits you have. What do you need to reach a multiple of 9?

sets.why: Multiples of 21: 21 (÷ 14? no), 42 (yes). The LCM is 42, not 294.
sets.no: List the multiples of the bigger number: ×1, ×2, ×3… Stop at the first one the smaller number also divides evenly.

sets.q: One sprinkler turns on every 12 minutes and another every 16 minutes. They just turned on together. In how many minutes will they turn on together again?
sets.why: Multiples of 16: 16 (÷ 12? no), 32 (no), 48 (yes). The LCM is 48 minutes.
sets.no: List the multiples of the bigger number: ×1, ×2, ×3… Stop at the first one the smaller number also divides evenly.

sets.q: Dad has 27 apples and 63 oranges. He packs identical fruit bags with nothing left over. What is the greatest number of bags?
sets.why: Factors of 27: 1, 3, 9, 27. 63 ÷ 9 = 7, but 63 ÷ 27 leaves 9. The GCF is 9 bags (3 apples and 7 oranges in each).
no: 3 is a common factor, but 9 is greater.
189 is the LCM, a multiple. You can't make 189 bags from 27 apples.

sets.q: 7 is a factor of 63, so 63 is a ________ of 7.
sets.why: 63 is a multiple of 7 (7 × 9).

visual.text:
Read the story
The Bird Feeder
1 Dad held up a milk jug with a hole cut in its side. “This will be our bird feeder,” he said.
2 “Birds won’t come to a milk jug,” Ethan said.
3 “Fill it with seeds and wait,” Dad said.
4 The next morning, three cardinals were eating from it. “I take it back!” Ethan laughed.

choices: “This will be our bird feeder,” Dad said.
“This will be our bird feeder”, Dad said.
“This will be our bird feeder.” Dad said.
“this will be our bird feeder,” Dad said.
sets.why: Tag last: comma inside the closing mark, capital on the first spoken word.
no: The comma belongs inside the closing quotation mark.
A period ends it too early. The tag finishes the sentence, so use a comma.
The first spoken word, This, needs a capital.

sets.q: “Do we need more seeds__” Ethan asked. What end mark goes in the blank, inside the quotation marks? Type its name.
sets.why: He is asking, so a question mark goes inside: “Do we need more seeds?” Ethan asked.
sets.no: Look at the tag: Ethan asked.
sets.hint: It is not a period or a comma.
